notes: Explore idea: measure the README-admitted 'not a joint optimum' gap of the TOU battery plan on real meters, then close it. Data: OPSD household_data 2020-04-15 (CC BY 4.0), 5 Konstanz buildings, 57 complete building-months x 3 illustrative tariffs x 4 battery sizes = 684 cases, HiGHS (SciPy) LP as reference. Two-step plan captured 100.0% / 94.6% / 93.4% of the optimal saving (demand-heavy / both-demand / energy-heavy), worst month 7.94% of bill; >1% of bill in 78 of 456 TOU cases. Shipped lp.mjs: dependency-free Mehrotra IPM with banded normal equations + Woodbury for the two cap columns + iterative refinement; jointLP candidate in planMonth. After: all 684 within $0.03 of HiGHS; joint kept in 559, peak-shaving ties in 125. 0.15-0.44 s per month in Node; example page (4 months) 1.1 s in headless Chromium, no console errors. Verification: node --test *.test.mjs 36/36 (run_venture_tests.py demand-charge-interval-analyzer ok); check/joint_gap.py results committed. Next: put the ratchet inside the optimisation (multi-month LP), or a forecast-based controller to replace the perfect-foresight bound.
